briefing.text: SCLC subtypes SCLC-A, SCLC-N and SCLC-P are defined by RNA or protein (IHC) expression of the transcription factors ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3, not by any DNA mutation or copy-number change. Before choosing a label, list every file and column provided and search them (case-insensitive) for mRNA expression, IHC scores or a subtype annotation (ascl1, neurod, pou2f3, subtype). If such a variable exists, call subtypes per sample with a relative-expression rule (highest of the TFs) and report mixed ASCL1/NEUROD1 calls rather than forcing absence.
briefing.reason: Whether a subtype-defining variable exists in the tables is the deciding question for which label the task rules allow; teams must check for it explicitly rather than infer subtype from genomic tables.

briefing.text: ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 may not be on the targeted sequencing panel used here; check whether they appear in data_cna.txt, the Hugo_Symbol column of data_mutations.txt and the panel in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. A gene missing from these tables means it was not measured, not that the subtype is absent.
briefing.reason: Prevents misreading missing measurement as a negative result about subtype presence.

briefing.text: MYC-family amplification (MYCL, MYC, MYCN) is only loosely associated with SCLC subtypes, and most SCLCs carry none, so CNA cannot assign or exclude a subtype for a sample. If tabulated, treat it as indirect context only, not as grounds for a True/False label.
briefing.reason: Stops teams from using a weak genomic proxy as if it measured subtype.

briefing.text: The cohort mixes PDX model samples and patient tumour samples (see SAMPLE_CLASS in data_clinical_sample.txt), and SAMPLE_TYPE values differ in case (e.g. Metastasis/metastasis). The hypothesis concerns PDX/CDX models only: filter by SAMPLE_CLASS and normalise case before counting anything.
briefing.reason: Any analysis must be restricted to the model samples the hypothesis is about.

briefing.text: Decide the label strictly from what the given tables contain, following the task's label definitions; do not use published knowledge about SCLC models to assign a label the data themselves do not support.
briefing.reason: Keeps the judgement grounded in the data rather than prior beliefs about the literature.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed SCLC-A/N/P subtype can only be established from RNA/IHC of ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3, and that DNA-level panel data (CNA, mutations, SV, histology) carry no admissible evidence; neither tested whether any variable in the data acts as a documented proxy.

Both teams treated SAMPLE_CLASS == 'PDX' as the full set of models in scope; the hypothesis names PDX/CDX, and no CDX class exists, yet 8 'PDX' samples have PROCEDURE_TYPE 'Blood Draw' / TISSUE_SITE 'blood' (likely circulating-tumour-cell-derived). Neither team checked whether CDX models are hidden inside the PDX class.
Both teams assumed that absence of the three gene names from every table means 'not measured' rather than 'measured and not altered'; neither checked per-panel gene coverage across IMPACT341/410/468.
unused_evidence: PROCEDURE_TYPE and TISSUE_SITE (Blood Draw / blood for 8 xenografts): bears on whether CDX models are present, which defines the population the hypothesis is about.

CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED / ONCOTREE_CODE: 2 PDX samples are Combined Small Cell Lung Carcinoma, and patient tumours include LCNEC and lung neuroendocrine tumour; histology is a neighbouring but distinct axis from TF subtype, and neither team stated why it is or is not relevant.
YAP1 row in data_cna.txt (the marker of a proposed fourth, non-neuroendocrine subtype) and neuroendocrine-related genes: unused; may be indirect context only.
Matched patient 'Tumor' samples (27) and the timeline files: unused; would matter only under a reading that compares models with their source tumours.
data_gene_panel_matrix.txt per-sample panel versions: neither team reported whether ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 are on any of the three panel versions, i.e. whether absence is structural.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A's weakest point (whether indirect genomic evidence would count) was resolved only by judgement, not by checking whether any provided variable is a recognised proxy for TF subtype.
Team B's weakest point (the hypothesis likely derives from IHC/RNA data not supplied) was reported, not resolved; Team B listed no pitfalls checked.
Neither team distinguished 'gene not on panel' from 'gene on panel but unaltered' using the gene panel definitions.
second_readings: 'PDX/CDX models' could mean all xenografts including CTC-derived ones; the scope question changes which samples are examined, though not obviously whether a subtype variable exists.

'Not present' is an absence claim; a reader could argue that missing evidence of presence supports it (True). The teams should state explicitly why absence of measurement does not count as evidence of absence.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed answer moderately to well. I confirmed that no expression, IHC or subtype variable exists and that the three genes are absent from all tables. The remaining risks are scope (CDX models hidden in the PDX class) and whether the teams justified treating the absence claim as unsettleable rather than as supported; neither risk looks likely to introduce a subtype variable.

findings.question: Are the transcription factor genes ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 included among the target genes of widely used hybrid-capture clinical tumour-sequencing panels of roughly 340-470 genes?
findings.answer: No, for MSK-IMPACT, the standard ~341/410/468-gene hybrid-capture panel. ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3 (and INSM1) are absent from all three versions; YAP1, MYCL, NKX2-1 and SOX2 are present. So in IMPACT-derived mutation/CNA tables, absence of ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 means 'not measured', not 'no alteration'. Other vendors' panels were not checked; the study's data_gene_panel_matrix.txt shows which panel was used.

QUESTION: Are the transcription factor genes ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 included among the target genes of widely used hybrid-capture clinical tumour-sequencing panels of roughly 340-470 genes? ANSWER: No, for MSK-IMPACT, the standard ~341/410/468-gene hybrid-capture panel. ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3 (and INSM1) are absent from all three versions; YAP1, MYCL, NKX2-1 and SOX2 are present. So in IMPACT-derived mutation/CNA tables, absence of ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 means 'not measured', not 'no alteration'. Other vendors' panels were not checked; the study's data_gene_panel_matrix.txt shows which panel was used. HOW SURE: high. SOURCES: https://github.com/idekerlab/MutationProjector/blob/4fec1265/data/gene/MSK-IMPACT468.txt, https://www.thelancet.com/cms/10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00104-7/attachment/93631f3d-043d-42b8-b9b4-c0df6cc9a5cb/mmc1.pdf.

findings.question: Is there any validated method to infer small cell lung cancer transcriptional subtypes (ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3/YAP1-defined) from DNA-only data, such as targeted-panel mutations or copy number, without RNA or IHC?
findings.answer: Not from mutations or copy number. A 2024 review states that no broad SCLC subtypes have been identified from mutational profiles and that mutation-based cfDNA profiling has not proved useful for subtyping. The only validated DNA-based approach is DNA methylation (tumour or cfDNA methylome classifiers, e.g. Heeke et al., Cancer Cell 2024). Panel mutation/CNA/SV/segment tables hold no methylation data, so they hold no recognised subtype proxy.

findings.question: In public cancer-genomics portals, how are circulating-tumour-cell-derived xenografts (CDX) usually encoded in sample-class fields? Are they typically lumped under 'PDX'/'xenograft'?
findings.answer: Yes, in cBioPortal. Its datahub curation rules allow SAMPLE_CLASS only the values 'Tumor', 'Cell Line' or 'Xenograft', so there is no CDX category and CTC-derived xenografts fall under Xenograft/PDX-type classes. They can be told apart only through other fields (e.g. specimen source = blood/CTC, or the sample ID). In SCLC literature, CDX means CTC-derived xenograft, a patient-derived model alongside tissue PDX. Elsewhere, CDX often means cell line-derived xenograft. I found no portal-wide rule beyond cBioPortal's, so how a given study fills its own free-text class field is not settled by the web.
